npc_ferryman.speaker: The Ferryman
default: Evening, traveler. You'd be the Wilted Flower, then — the one they whisper about on the bank.
The river's sick. Blight chokes the upstream bend, and the fish die belly-up in the reeds.
Clear the upstream Blight for me and I'll pole you across. It's the only road north.
quest_active: The taint thickens where the river bends north. Clear the Blight that chokes it.
Mind the Poison Nodes — they feed the sickness. The old Light Shrines may still guard you.
quest_cleared_light: The water runs clean again. The Light you carried kept the dark at bay, traveler.
quest_cleared_poison: The water runs clean again… though something in your eyes has grown colder than the river.
high_corruption: You carry the Blight now, like driftwood soaked through. Careful it doesn't carry you.
high_virtue: The Light clings to you like morning mist. The shrines will remember your name.

npc_lantern_keeper.speaker: The Lantern Keeper
default: A lamp for the lost. That's all I keep out here on the water's edge.
The dark out past the village isn't empty, traveler. It watches. Keep your lantern close.
quest_active: You're after the upstream Blight, aren't you? Then don't let your light gutter out.
The Shrines were lit long before the Blight came. Some of their warmth still waits to be woken.
quest_cleared_light: You brought the light back. The river has its shine again — I can feel it from here.
quest_cleared_poison: The river is clear… but your lamp burns a stranger color now. Mind the wick.
high_corruption: Your lantern gutters green. I've only ever seen that in the things that crawl out of the Blight.
high_virtue: You burn warm and steady. Whatever waits in the dark will think twice tonight.

npc_herbalist.speaker: The Herbalist
default: Sit. Breathe. The marsh reeks worse than usual — that's the Blight pushing south.
I gather what I can before the rot takes the roots. Not much clean medicine left up here.
quest_active: If you're wading upstream, take care — the Blight doesn't just poison the water, it poisons the blood.
A Poison Node is a festering wound in the earth. Absorb it and you carry its sickness in your own veins.
quest_cleared_light: The river runs clear and the herbs grow straight again. You've done a rare kindness.
quest_cleared_poison: You smell of rot and neon, friend. Sit still — let me at least try to draw some of it out.
high_corruption: Your pulse runs hot and green. That much Blight in a body… it usually hollows a person out.
high_virtue: There's a warmth in you that doesn't come from any fire I know. It suits you.

npc_elder.speaker: The Elder
default: The village remembers when the river ran clear and the shrine-lights burned till dawn.
Now the Shrines sleep cold and the young ones forget why we ever lit them at all.
quest_active: So the Ferryman has set you to the old work. Good. Someone must remember it.
Purify a Shrine and its warmth returns to the water. That is the old bargain, kept.
quest_cleared_light: You have restored the old warmth. The village owes you more than it knows how to say.
quest_cleared_poison: You traded the Blight's poison for the river's. I pray the bargain you struck was worth it.
high_corruption: The Blight has its hooks in you, child. Even so, the village will not turn you away.
high_virtue: The shrine-light follows you. You walk like the keepers of the old days.

npc_sibling.speaker: Your Sibling
default: You came back. I told them you would.
Don't wander too far upriver alone. Last time… last time the water kept what it took.
quest_active: You're going to the upstream bend? Then I'm coming with you as far as the shallows.
Be careful around the Poison Nodes. I've seen what they do to hands that get too close.
quest_cleared_light: You did it. The water's clear again — I can see the stones at the bottom, like when we were small.
quest_cleared_poison: You're different now. I'm glad you're back… but I miss the way you used to laugh.
high_corruption: Your hands are cold. And your eyes… don't look at me like that. Please.
high_virtue: You glow a little, you know. Like the lantern you carry never went out.
